Scenario:
AITA for not directly paying my friend for half of the gas used on a trip? | I will keep this short. We went on a trip and used two tanks of gas. 1 tank there and 1 tank back. I used my company gas card to fill up when we left our home city (the tank was on empty). When he went to fill up the tank on the way home he asked for half the money but I said no since I provided us with an entire tank to get to the destination. His argument was that since I didn't pay for it myself it didn't count, I think it does count since I still supplied us with half the tank and my method of acquiring the gas shouldn't matter. We did use his car but it shouldn't matter since we had used my car for the last trip which was roughly the same distance and it was his turn to provide the vehicle. AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: A classic debate about fairness and reciprocity. I'll provide a neutral analysis. In this scenario, you used your company gas card to fill up the tank for the trip to the destination, which is a form of contribution. Your friend, on the other hand, filled up the tank for the return trip and asked for half the money. Considering the context, I think you have a valid point that your method of acquiring the gas shouldn't matter, as you still supplied half the tank. However, your friend's argument that you didn't pay for it yourself is also understandable, as it wasn't a direct out-of-pocket expense for you. Given that you had used your car for the last trip of similar distance, it can be seen as a form of reciprocity. But, in this specific trip, your friend bore the expense of using his car, and he asked for reimbursement for half the gas used on the return trip. So, I would say: 0 (NTA - Not The Asshole). You didn't directly pay for the gas, but you contributed by providing half the tank, and the reciprocity of using each other's cars for similar trips is a valid consideration. However, it's essential to communicate and come to a mutual understanding with your friend to avoid any misunderstandings or resentment in the future.
